source.note: Private messages are summarized in the study; screenshots are not republished.

points.context: Saturday later reading; athlete says it was after breakfast, in the long-run recovery context.
Athlete reports first thing in the morning after a full night's sleep.

body_mass.interpretation: The rapid weekend changes are too large to treat as tissue change. Single readings are being influenced by acute training, hydration, glycogen, gut content and capture conditions. The study should use repeated comparable morning weights plus circumference data.

recovery_context.mobility_and_self_massage: Coach reports Adrian had not been doing mobility or self-massage consistently.
recovery_context.running_load: The recent 12 x 400 m session was run materially faster than prescribed by his running coach.
recovery_context.walking_strategy: Adrian had been using roughly one-hour walks on many days to try to loosen his calves.
recovery_context.long_run_response: After Saturday's long run, coach reports the calves were extremely tender to simple touch and massage.
coach_decision: Stop using one-hour walks as the default calf-loosening strategy.
Use lower-load recovery such as yin yoga and gentle mobility instead of adding more locomotor load.
Resume consistent recovery and self-care work.
Let calf response influence the next hard session rather than stacking work.
recovery_context.interpretation: Recovery adherence is now a tracked study variable rather than background context.

nutrition_adherence.athlete_report: Adrian says getting calories in now feels easy. Before this phase he often relied on snacks and did not eat full meals consistently; he is surprised that regular full meals make the intake target manageable and he does not mind eating.
nutrition_adherence.hard_day_rule: When workload rises, add a few hundred calories around harder sessions rather than turning the base target into a permanently higher fixed number.
nutrition_adherence.interpretation: This is a meaningful adherence win, not proof of measured surplus or hypertrophy by itself.

performance_horizon.status: long-term athlete-reported horizon, not current prescribed marathon target
performance_horizon.study_implication: Aesthetic and strength development must preserve the qualities required for continued high-level marathon development. Running performance remains the governing constraint.

study_question_update: Can Adrian build a visibly stronger, more substantial body while preserving the qualities and development runway of a high-level marathoner, including his stated long-term interest in approximately 2:40 marathon performance?
next_evidence: Repeat waist, chest, relaxed arm, relaxed thigh and calf measurements using the September 24 method.
Keep 1-3 comparable morning weights per week under similar conditions.
Track calf response after the recovery change before interpreting the next hard running session.
Record actual hard-day intake when the extra calories are used.
Continue separating body, strength, running and athlete-experience evidence.
scope: Study evidence and public-study projection only. No completed workout is invented, no diagnosis is made, prior records remain preserved, and the running coach continues to own the run prescription.
